parole.significato: An ancient Persian plucked lute with a pear-shaped body, a flat belly, an angled back near the pegbox, and a fretless n…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Persian بربط (barbat, barbot), from Middle Persian, possibly from Ancient Greek βάρβιτος (bárbitos), an unrelated musical instrument.

parole.significato: A small-land-owning citizen of the Sassanian Empire.
parole.testo: From Persian دهقان (dehqân, “landowner”) From Middle Persian 𐭣𐭧𐭩𐭥𐭪𐭠𐭭 (dahigān, “countryman, farmer”), originally meaning “pertaining to the Deh”, from Middle Persian 𐭬𐭲𐭠 (deh, “country, land, village”).

parole.significato: A symbol of the religion Zoroastrianism, also used to represent the Iranian nation.
parole.testo: From Persian فروهر (faravahar), from Middle Persian plwʾhl.
From Persian خیار (xiyâr, “cucumber”), derived from Middle Persian 𐭧𐭩𐭠𐭥 (xyār). Cognate to Sanskrit क्षीरक (kṣīraka).

parole.significato: A Revolutionary Guard (member of the Army of the Guardians of the Islamic Revolution)
parole.testo: From Persian پاسداران, plural of پاسدار (“guard, sentinel, watchman”), from داشتن پاس 'to keep a watch', from Middle Persian, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂- and *dʰer-.

parole.significato: A king of Persia or Iran.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Persian شاه (šâh), from Middle Persian 𐭬𐭫𐭪𐭠 (šāh), from Old Persian 𐏋 (XŠ /⁠xšāyaθiya⁠/). Doublet of check. More at chess.

parole.significato: A now-extinct branch of Zoroastrianism that had the divinity Zurvan as its primordial creator deity.
parole.testo: Of Persian origin, Zurvan + -ism, from Middle Persian [script needed] (Zurvān), from Avestan 𐬰𐬭𐬎𐬎𐬁𐬥 (zruuān, “time”).
